parts.visual:
A great product with a bad launch will fail. Executives design the GTM (Go-To-Market) Strategy before the product is even finished.

The GTM Pillars:
1. Target Audience: Exactly who is buying this?
2. Positioning: Why is it better than the competition?
3. Distribution Channels: How will we sell it (Direct, Partners, Online)?
4. Pricing: How much will it cost?
parts.audio: A great product with a bad launch will fail. You must design a Go-To-Market Strategy that defines the audience, positioning, channels, and pricing.

questions.question: What happens if a company launches a product without a clear 'Target Audience'?
options: They waste millions on marketing because their messaging is generic and appeals to no one specifically.
questions.correct_answer: They waste millions on marketing because their messaging is generic and appeals to no one specifically.
questions.explanation: If you try to sell to everyone, you end up selling to no one. Niche focus is critical for a launch.

questions.question: Listen to the marketing VP. What part of the GTM strategy is this?
questions.tts_text: We will not sell this software directly to consumers. We are going to license it exclusively through enterprise consulting firms.
questions.explanation: A distribution channel is the method you use to get your product into the hands of the end-user.

questions.question: What is 'Positioning'?
options: Where you put the product on the shelf.
The specific mental space you want your product to occupy in the minds of your target audience compared to competitors.
questions.correct_answer: The specific mental space you want your product to occupy in the minds of your target audience compared to competitors.
questions.explanation: Positioning is answering: 'We are the fastest,' or 'We are the most secure,' or 'We are the luxury option.'

questions.question: Why is 'Sales Enablement' a critical part of a GTM launch?
options: Because the sales team needs to be trained, given scripts, and understand the product perfectly before the launch date.
To give the sales team a vacation.
questions.correct_answer: Because the sales team needs to be trained, given scripts, and understand the product perfectly before the launch date.
questions.explanation: A GTM strategy fails if Marketing generates leads, but Sales doesn't know how to sell the new product.

pairs.match: How a product is perceived in the market
The method of delivering the product to customers
The specific group of consumers a product is aimed at
